newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron shares fall on market share talk.
newsitem.headline: Petron shares fall on market share talk.

text.p: Shares of Petron Corp fell by 30 centavos to 9.60 pesos in early trade on Monday on talk of a declining market share for domestic refiners as the oil industry deregulates, brokers said.

"There's some concern that Petron and the other oil refiners may not be able to sustain their market positions with the entry of other companies," said Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities.
Traders said the institutional selling of Petron shares in early trade was also part of the general trend of investors moving out of blue chips to secondliners.
"There are people shifting out of blue chips to secondliners. Last week, there was selling of Meralco shares and this week, its Petron's turn," Ferrer added.

Petron officials were not immediately available for comment but company chairman Monico Jacob has previously expressed confidence Petron will maintain its current market share of more than 40 percent despite deregulation.
